title: Accessibility triage
question: I have hundreds of a11y issues — where do I actually start?
what: Ranks accessibility issues by severity × reach and returns a top-N action list.
benefit: Converts an unreadable issue dump into three things to fix this afternoon.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Manual-fixes checklist
question: What is left for a human after the auto-fixers have run?
what: Audits, dry-runs every fixer, then reports only what survives — grouped and prioritised.
benefit: An honest to-do list for the last mile to 100%, so nobody promises a score the tools cannot reach.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Lyra visual patterns
question: What is a correctly-converted Lyra page supposed to look like?
what: Reference for Lyra page chrome, surfaces, tables, panels, nav, chips and AI affordances in light and dark.
benefit: Load it before any conversion and you know what you are going to get — no surprise redesigns.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Figma element → CSS
question: What is the CSS for this layer?
what: Turns the selected Figma node into production CSS with Lyra tokens substituted where they match.
benefit: Output that survives a theme change, instead of hard-coded hex and px.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Browser element → spec sheet
question: What are the design specs of this element on the page?
what: Pulls computed CSS for the inspected element and annotates every raw value with its nearest token.
benefit: A spec a developer can act on, not just a description of what is there.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Figma ↔ Chrome parity
question: Does the live site actually match the Figma?
what: Aligns Figma layers to page elements by name and diffs colors, type, spacing, radius and shadows.
benefit: Ends the "it looks off but I cannot say why" review with a per-property drift table.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Artboard → live page
question: Can we make this real page look like this artboard?
what: Maps artboard styling onto page selectors and applies it as CSS overrides after you confirm the mapping.
benefit: Demo a redesign on the real product in minutes, with no branch and no build.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Dark-mode parity
question: Does this page work in dark mode, or only in light?
what: Audits colors in light, simulates dark, audits again, and always restores the baseline.
benefit: Only the delta — what breaks in dark and what breaks in light. No re-reading the full audit.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Token candidates
question: Which of these custom values should just become Lyra tokens?
what: Groups recurring raw values across all four domains and ranks the ones worth promoting.
benefit: Fixes the cause once upstream instead of the same symptom on thirty screens.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Ten-question UX eval
question: Is this good enough to move to the next step, or to dev?
what: Answers all ten prioritisation questions against real evidence, then states pass / pass-with-conditions / not-yet. For AI-surface designs, also layers in the North Star Fox tenet check.
benefit: A defensible verdict with the reasoning attached — the thing you can actually take to a VP.
author: Bill Bangs

title: North Star Fox
question: Does this design or JIRA ticket actually hold up against our AI-first tenets?
what: Scores a CXone AI design, screen, or JIRA ticket against the twelve NiCE AI design tenets, plus Lyra Foundations and NiCE Brand adherence, and returns a fixed-shape pass/fail verdict per section.
benefit: A critical look at designs and JIRA tickets to ensure alignment with our Core Values around AI architecture at NiCE.
author: Janet Gonzales

title: NiCE product knowledge
question: What does this NICE product actually do, and who uses it?
what: Sourced reference on NICE the company and its product lines (CXone Mpower, Enlighten AI, Actimize, Evidencentral) — compiled from public material with citations.
benefit: Design decisions grounded in what the real product and its real users are, instead of generic SaaS assumptions.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Team strengths
question: Who should I put on this, and what will this group get wrong?
what: The design team's CliftonStrengths grid (45 people, top 10 themes each) plus the analysis: lookup, group composition, find-the-person matching, and 1:1 coaching prep.
benefit: Staffing and 1:1 decisions grounded in how people actually work, instead of who was free.
author: NiCE Designer

title: EAC Framework Guide
question: Which tenet does this fall under, and what do I actually show my manager?
what: The eight Personal behaviors cards from the Engagement Orchestration PM framework: purpose, capabilities, and the verbatim 'show your manager' column, plus routing, calibration prep, self-assessment and manager-side calibration.
benefit: Turns a framework you skim once into the specific instance you bring to your next 1:1.
author: EAC Team

title: Research planning
question: What method answers this question, and what do I actually ask?
what: Matches a research question to a method, then writes the brief, discussion guide, or screener it needs. Carries the JTBD switching-interview structure and survey/SUS design as reference files.
benefit: A study someone else could run, anchored to the decision it informs instead of to what was easy to schedule.
author: Serena Yang

title: Research synthesis
question: I have the sessions back. What does this actually say?
what: Thematic analysis, affinity mapping, personas and journey maps from submitted data, split into convergent patterns, contradictions, and thin signals rather than one flat list.
benefit: Findings traceable to the data behind them, with the contradictions named instead of averaged into a "mixed reception" theme.
author: Serena Yang

title: Research readouts
question: How do I get this in front of stakeholders without it getting waved off?
what: Readouts, exec summaries, decks, HTML deliverables and flow diagrams, plus audience tailoring and the writing standards that apply to every research artifact.
benefit: A readout that leads with the conclusion and preempts the three objections every research review gets.
author: Serena Yang

title: Clean web page extraction
question: Can you just give me the article, not the whole page?
what: Uses the Defuddle CLI to strip navigation, ads, and clutter from a web page and return clean markdown.
benefit: Cuts token usage on any URL fetch that is not already markdown, without losing the actual content.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Prompt guru
question: Is this prompt actually going to get me what I want?
what: Reviews a vague or under-specified prompt, rewrites it, explains the improvement, and runs the better version.
benefit: Catches ambiguity before it burns a turn on the wrong answer.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Emotional intelligence voice & tone
question: Does this read as clear and human, or defensive and corporate?
what: A voice-and-tone guide for leadership writing, feedback, reviews, and difficult conversations — clarity, reasoning over assertion, and named reactions before responses.
benefit: Writing that lands as thoughtful and credible instead of performative or tone-deaf.
author: Megan Fisher

title: UI bug hunter
question: What is wrong with this screenshot?
what: Runs a structured 9-layer visual QA pass over a screenshot, image, or recording and produces Jira-style tickets for every real issue.
benefit: A bug list ready to file, not a paragraph of impressions.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Obsidian power user
question: Can you just build this directly in my Obsidian vault?
what: Produces the actual Obsidian artifact — notes, canvases, bases, Dataview queries, Templater templates, vault structures, CSS snippets — for any vault request.
benefit: One skill for the whole vault, so a request does not have to be pre-sorted into canvas vs. base vs. note.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Obsidian-flavored markdown
question: How do I write this note so Obsidian's extensions actually work?
what: Wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties, and the other Obsidian-specific Markdown extensions beyond standard CommonMark.
benefit: Notes that render correctly in Obsidian the first time, not after a round of fixing broken syntax.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Obsidian Bases
question: Can I get a database-style view of these notes?
what: Creates and edits .base files — filters, formulas, table/card/list/map views.
benefit: A working Base on the first try, since Base YAML fails silently on quoting mistakes.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Obsidian CLI
question: Can you drive my actual running Obsidian instance?
what: Reads, creates, and searches vault notes via the Obsidian CLI, plus plugin/theme development commands (reload, run JS, screenshot, inspect DOM). Requires Obsidian to be open.
benefit: Vault operations that touch the live app, not just files on disk.
author: NiCE Designer

title: JSON Canvas
question: Can you lay this out as an Obsidian canvas / mind map?
what: Creates and edits .canvas files per the JSON Canvas 1.0 spec — nodes, edges, groups, connections.
benefit: A canvas file that opens correctly in Obsidian, not just visually-plausible JSON.
author: NiCE Designer

title: Meeting → design brief
question: I have raw discovery notes — can you turn this into something I can actually design from?
what: Layer 1 of the ideation pipeline: transforms raw meeting notes or transcripts into a structured Design Brief.
benefit: A brief the next three pipeline stages can consume, instead of a wall of meeting notes.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Fast research pack
question: What has already been tried here, and what patterns should this borrow from?
what: Layer 2 of the ideation pipeline: generates analogous solutions, design patterns, competitive landscape, UX heuristics, and anti-patterns from a Design Brief.
benefit: Replaces a day or two of secondary research with a few minutes, grounded in the actual brief.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Proposal generator
question: Can you give me a few genuinely different directions, not just one idea?
what: Layer 3 of the ideation pipeline: generates Conservative / Progressive / Disruptive proposals from a Design Brief and Research Pack, each with concept, journey, screen inventory, and a scoring matrix.
benefit: A real choice between directions with trade-offs spelled out, instead of one idea to react to.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Wireframe generator
question: Can I get a clickable prototype out of this proposal?
what: Layer 4a of the ideation pipeline: generates a self-contained, annotated, responsive HTML wireframe prototype from a design proposal.
benefit: Something to click through and react to, not just a static description of the screens.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Push proposal to Figma
question: Can you get this proposal into Figma as real frames?
what: Layer 4b of the ideation pipeline: pushes proposal screens into Figma via the Figma MCP as named, auto-laid-out frames bound to design tokens.
benefit: A structured proposal page in the actual design file, ready for a designer to refine instead of rebuild.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Design ops
question: How should my whole team run this, not just how do I do it once?
what: Builds reusable team process for design leads: critique frameworks, sprint planning, handoff process, onboarding plans, working agreements, program reviews.
benefit: A process the team runs every sprint, not a one-off answer that has to be re-derived next time.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Design research
question: What research method fits this question, and how do I run it end to end?
what: Research planning, interview guides, usability test plans, synthesis, personas, journey maps, card sorting, tree testing, and survey analysis, plus method selection.
benefit: One answer for "how do I find out" across the whole research lifecycle, not just the write-up stage.
author: Yaara Bar

title: UX strategy
question: What is our north star, and how does it tie to the business?
what: Design principles, UX vision documents, experience maps, and problem framing that connect user needs to business outcomes.
benefit: A strategic artifact that aligns a team for months, not a single decision for one project.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Product thinking partner
question: Can you push back on this instead of just agreeing with me?
what: A dialogue protocol for product/research/UX work that pressure-tests claims, separates evidence from hypothesis, and challenges framing before it goes in a document.
benefit: Catches the bias and the unexamined assumption before it ships in a deck, not after.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Prism
question: I have messy notes and a blank page — help me think this through.
what: Turns raw product inputs into decision-quality thinking and writing: synthesis, positioning, competitive analysis, prioritization, PRDs, stakeholder updates, and strategy briefs.
benefit: Structured product thinking before structured product writing, so the document is not built on an unexamined claim.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Figma → developer a11y instructions
question: Can you write the accessibility spec for this screen so a developer can just build it?
what: Produces a fixed-style HTML accessibility spec from a Figma screen URL: semantic structure, tab order, keyboard patterns, screen-reader text, and a color/contrast table with WCAG-passing recommendations.
benefit: A polished, consistent a11y handoff doc per screen instead of a one-off markdown list that looks different every time.
author: Yaara Bar

title: Research lead operating system
question: How do I run a small research team without the process becoming a second job?
what: A minimum-viable-rigor operating system for a one-person research lead: three effort-scaled modes, an evidence chain, a decision brief, and a shared knowledge base.
benefit: The lightest process that still produces a traceable, falsifiable decision — scaled to the size of the question, not a fixed heavyweight ritual.
author: Yaara Bar

title: NiCE Present
question: Can you build me a deck for this, right here in the chat?
what: Creates a polished, NiCE-branded internal presentation as a self-contained interactive HTML slide deck rendered inline — pitches, exec updates, project briefs, roadmap and team updates.
benefit: A presentable deck in the conversation itself, with no separate slide tool round-trip.
author: Yaara Bar

title: PM Brain
question: Can you set me up a second brain for this product, not just answer one question about it?
what: Scaffolds a markdown-native second brain for a product operator: detects greenfield vs. migration, runs an interview, populates a deterministic folder structure, and self-tests.
benefit: A durable, searchable home for judgment-heavy product work instead of scattered docs and chat history.
author: Yaara Bar
